The 2-of-3 CHECKMULTISIG script places keys in fixed positional order user, backup, BitGo with no BIP67 sorting (p2ms receives the triple as-is; the published repo fixture is not in sorted order). deprecated p2tr type: script-path leaves are 2-of-2 all-sign CHECKSIGVERIFY chains over key pairs (user,bitgo) at tree depth 1 and (user,backup), (backup,bitgo) at depth 2. Leaf template is per revealed leaf; key-path spends of the aggregated pair are indistinguishable from single-key spends and this study never attributes from them.

p2trMusig2 type: key path over the MuSig2 aggregate of user and BitGo keys (appears as single-key single-signature on chain per BitGo's own docs), with 2-of-2 leaves (user,backup) and (backup,bitgo) both at tree depth 1. Key-path spends are outside attribution scope; only revealed leaves match the template.

The v0 service key is a network-level constant published in the gdk source (service_pubkey), so v0 scripts are provider-static: the same server pubkey recurs across all v0 accounts. Server key sits first in the script; keys unsorted (flags 0).

expected_structures.structure_notes: csv address type (2of2 with recovery): the wally optimized layout used on Bitcoin mainnet is recovery_pubkey OP_CHECKSIGVERIFY main_pubkey OP_CHECKSIG OP_IFDUP OP_NOTIF <csv_blocks> OP_CSV OP_ENDIF, so a normal spend shows two signatures and the expired path shows the user key alone after the CSV delay. csv_blocks is chosen from the mainnet buckets 25920, 51840, 65535 (valid range 17 to 65535). The classifier labels this shape other with family timelocked_singlesig_recovery because there is no OP_CHECKMULTISIG. This exact template with 51840 is one of the most distinctive provider shapes in the registry.

expected_structures.structure_notes: collaborative/assisted wallets default to NATIVE_SEGWIT m-of-n (2-of-3 in the published BSMS example) with the Nunchuk platform signer occupying the last key slot. sortedmulti vs multi is caller-chosen in the open-source descriptor code, so sortedness is not attributable from public sources; either choice yields the same L3 template. LEGACY (P2SH) and NESTED_SEGWIT (P2SH-P2WSH) address types are also selectable.

taproot wallets are supported: multi_a/sortedmulti_a script paths, MuSig2 key-path descriptors tr(musig(...)), and a DISABLE_KEY_PATH template with an unspendable internal key. Which variant a given wallet uses is customer-chosen and nothing structural is pinned publicly; key-path MuSig2 spends are single-signature on chain and outside attribution scope.

inheritance/assisted templates: 2-of-4 before the timelock with the platform key as slot 4, degrading to 1-of-3 after it (3-of-5 to 2-of-4 variants also shipped in the desktop resources). Timelocks are OLDER (CSV) or AFTER (CLTV) miniscript nodes; concrete values and the miniscript template come from the Nunchuk server at runtime and are not published in any open-source repo.

sources.what: BIP67: compressed keys sorted lexicographically by binary representation so a key set has a canonical P2SH address; uncompressed keys incompatible. The BIP text covers P2SH only; P2WSH sorted multisig is the ecosystem extension (see Specter and Caravan code)

expected_structures.structure_notes: the generic canonical-order 2-of-3 that DIY wallets, exchange cold storage, and older services produce. Identical L3 to the BitGo and Unchained rows: the engine must use keys_sorted, form, and corroborating evidence to separate providers from this control, and this row quantifies the false-positive floor for the whole template.
